editorial:
Imagine being thrown into a place where the adults are just as mean as the kids. You follow Carlin, a tough new kid who arrives at a reform school already known for being a troublemaker. The vibe is gritty and raw, making you feel like you are stuck in those gray walls right along with the inmates. The guards don't actually want to help these boys; instead, they play mind games and encourage the gang leader, Pongo, to beat Carlin down. It is a brutal power struggle where you see how quickly the social ladder shifts as Carlin fights his way to the top to become the new boss of the ward.

What really hits hard is the acting, which feels so real it almost looks like a documentary. The pacing is steady, building up the tension until everything boils over into total chaos. While it can be hard to watch because of the violence, that is exactly why it works. If you like stories about survival and rebellion, you need to see this. It is a rough ride, but totally worth it.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a massive riot where the boys finally snap and attack the guards. After the violence settles, the authorities try to act like they are in control again. Carlin is the only one left standing strong. In the final scene, he realizes that the system is designed to make them fail. He accepts his role as a leader, but he knows he is still trapped in a cycle of pain and anger.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raw stories about power struggles and rebellion.
